name: STP16CPC26PTR
title: STP16CPC26: 16-channel constant-current LED sink driver with serial shift register, 3 V to 5.5 V
summary: Sixteen open-drain current sinks, each switched by one bit of a serial-in shift register and latch, drive LEDs at 5 mA to 90 mA per channel; one resistor on R-EXT sets the current for all of them. Data clocks in at up to 30 MHz, SDO lets devices be chained, and OE blanks or dims every output at once. The outputs stand off 20 V, the logic runs from 3 V to 5.5 V, and a 170 °C thermal shutdown turns the outputs off. Applications are video display panel LED drivers and special lighting; STP16CPC26PTR is the QSOP-24 version.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: Sixteen LEDs hang from a shared LED rail, one on each output, and each output pulls its LED's cathode down with the same regulated current. A single resistor from R-EXT to ground sets that current for all sixteen. The pattern arrives on SDI, CLK and LE from a controller, and a pulse train on OE dims all outputs together, from fully off to fully on.

parts.note: current-setting resistor; values in the Rext table

circuits.title: Test circuit for electrical characteristics
circuits.description: The bench set-up for the DC figures. A supply feeds VDD and its current IDD is measured; REXT to ground carries IREF and sets the output current. An adjustable source is switched onto OE, CLK, LE or SDI in turn to measure input levels and input currents. Every output and SDO is brought out so the output current IOL, the leakage and the SDO levels can be measured.

operation.text: On each rising CLK edge the level on SDI enters a 16-bit shift register and the oldest bit leaves on SDO, so several devices chain SDO to SDI on a common clock. CLK to SDO takes 30 ns typ at 3.3 V and 20 ns typ at 5 V. The clock runs to 30 MHz; SDI needs 5 ns setup and 10 ns hold around the clock edge.

LE and OE act on level, not on the clock. While LE is high the latches follow the shift register; when it falls they keep the last pattern. With OE low each output follows its latch bit (1 = on); with OE high all outputs are off and the latches are untouched. A full update is sixteen clocks of data followed by one LE pulse of at least 20 ns.
Brightness of all outputs is varied from 0 % to 100 % by pulsing OE. The shortest OE pulse is 150 ns; the OE to output delay is 100 ns typ for the output going from L to H and 25 ns typ for H to L.

One resistor from R-EXT to ground sets the same current in every output, from 5 mA to 90 mA: about 999 Ω for 20 mA and 217 Ω for 90 mA (table of Rext values, and the curve of Rext against current). Outputs match within ±1 % typ, ±3 % max, at 22 mA and 55 mA, and devices match within ±6 % max.

Each output needs a minimum voltage across it to stay in regulation, rising with current: 170 mV at 20 mA and 770 mV to 820 mV at 90 mA. The values are guidance, and a design should leave some margin above them. Outputs withstand 20 V when off, so a string of several LEDs in series fits on each channel.

At a junction temperature of 170 °C typ all outputs are switched off, whatever the latches hold. They come back on by themselves once the die has cooled by the hysteresis, 15 °C typ, and operation carries on.

Every logic input has clamp diodes to VDD and to ground and a 1 kΩ series resistor into a CMOS gate. OE also has a 500 kΩ pull-up to VDD and LE a 500 kΩ pull-down to ground. SDO is a CMOS push-pull stage from VDD with a diode to ground.

Output rise and fall times are taken between the 10 % and 90 % points of the output voltage, and turn-on gives no current overshoot. Delays and setup times are taken at the 50 % points of the signals.
On the TSSOP24 exposed pad version the pad goes to a copper land that is isolated or grounded; soldered down it lowers RthJA to 37.5 °C/W from 85 °C/W for the plain TSSOP24.
